title.en: World Desk
title.zh: 全球焦点

strap.en: A fast view of global affairs, conflict, diplomacy, and human need.
strap.zh: 快速掌握国际局势、冲突、外交与人类处境。

title.en: Tourists in England face nightly levy on hotel and Airbnb stays under new plans
title.zh: 英格兰酒店和爱彼迎住宿将面临新的夜间税

summary.en: Under new government plans, tourists in England will be subject to a nightly levy on hotel and Airbnb-style accommodations. This 'tourist tax' would empower mayors to decide how the collected revenue is invested, similar to a scheme already in place in Scotland.
summary.zh: 根据政府的新计划，英格兰的游客将在酒店和类似爱彼迎的住宿中面临每晚征收的费用。这项“旅游税”将赋予市长权力，让他们决定如何投资所筹集的收入，这与苏格兰已有的计划类似。

body.en: Labelled a tourist tax, proposals would give mayors power to decide how revenue raised should be invested Holidaymakers will face a nightly levy on hotel stays and Airbnb-style visits in England under plans ministers are due to outline to give mayors new powers. The idea, labelled a tourist tax, was first raised by Keir Starmer’s government in November and is similar to a scheme running in Scotland. It would allow mayors to charge a fee to visitors staying overnight and decide how the revenue raised should be invested. Continue reading...
body.zh: 被称为旅游税的提案将赋予市长决定如何投资所筹集的收入的权力。根据部长们将赋予市长新权力的计划，度假者将面临对英国酒店住宿和爱彼迎式访问的每晚征税。这个被称为旅游税的想法最初是由凯尔·斯塔默 (Keir Starmer) 政府于 11 月提出的，与苏格兰实施的计划类似。它将允许市长向过夜的游客收取费用，并决定如何投资所筹集的收入。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The proposed 'tourist tax' in England aims to generate revenue for local investment, echoing the ancient mandate for rulers to ensure justice and provide for their people. As Jeremiah 22:3 states, leaders are called to "execute justice and righteousness, and deliver from the hand of the oppressor him who suffers violence." May this new revenue stream truly...
reflection.zh: 英格兰拟议的“旅游税”旨在为当地投资创造收入，这呼应了古代统治者为人民伸张正义和提供保障的职责。正如耶利米书 22:3 所说，领袖被呼召要“施行公平和公义，拯救被欺压的脱离欺压者的手。”愿这笔新收入真正服务于社区和游客的福祉。

verse.textEn: Do what is just and right. Rescue from the hand of the oppressor the one who has been robbed.
verse.textZh: 你们要施行公平和公义，拯救被抢夺的脱离欺压人的手。

title.en: Russian drones kill at least nine in strikes targeting warehouses and ports in Ukraine – Europe live
title.zh: 俄无人机袭击乌克兰仓库和港口致至少九人死亡

summary.en: Russian drone strikes targeted warehouses and ports in Ukraine, resulting in at least nine deaths. This follows news that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's plane was nearly hit by a drone while departing Moldova. Separately, NATO allies reportedly thwarted a Russian attempt to deploy a secret weapon designed...
summary.zh: 俄罗斯无人机袭击了乌克兰的仓库和港口，造成至少九人死亡。此前有报道称，乌克兰总统弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基的飞机在离开摩尔多瓦时险些被一架无人机击中。另外，据报道，北约盟友挫败了一项俄罗斯试图部署旨在破坏海底电缆的秘密武器的计划。

body.en: The strikes come after it was revealed that Ukraine’s president Volodomyr Zelenskyy’s plane was almost hit by a drone when leaving Moldova this week Meanwhile, Reuters reported that Nato allies interrupted a Russian plot training to unleash a secret weapon designed to disable critical undersea cables without leaving any fingerprints. Two 1,400 km subsea fiber-optic cables linking Svalbard to mainland Norway lie as deep as 2,700 metres below the sea’s surface. They carry ⁠vast amounts of satellite data downloaded at the SvalSat satellite ground station, the world’s largest and part of NASA’s Near Space Network. Continue reading...
body.zh: 这次袭击是在乌克兰总统泽连斯基的飞机本周离开摩尔多瓦时差点被无人机击中之后发生的。与此同时，路透社报道称，北约盟国中断了俄罗斯的一次阴谋训练，以释放一种秘密武器，该武器旨在在不留下任何痕迹的情况下禁用关键的海底电缆。连接斯瓦尔巴群岛和挪威大陆的两条 1,400 公里长的海底光缆位于海面以下 2,700 米深处。它们携带着从 SvalSat 卫星地面站下载的大量卫星数据，该卫星地面站是世界上最大的卫星地面站，也是 NASA 近太空网络的一部分。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The news of drone strikes and near-misses paints a grim picture of escalating conflict. In such moments, the temptation to respond with equal force is strong. Yet, Scripture calls us to a higher path: 'Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.' This principle challenges us to seek ways to break the cycle of violence, even when faced with...
reflection.zh: 无人机袭击和险些被击中的消息描绘了一幅冲突升级的严峻图景。在这样的时刻，以牙还牙的冲动是强烈的。然而，圣经呼唤我们走上一条更高的道路：“不要被恶所胜，反要以善胜恶。”这一原则挑战我们，即使面对侵略，也要寻求打破暴力循环的方法。

verse.textEn: Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.
verse.textZh: 你不可为恶所胜，反要以善胜恶。

title.en: Tens of millions of people fail to get humanitarian aid as global system crumbles
title.zh: 全球系统崩溃，数千万人未能获得人道主义援助

summary.en: Funding cuts in 2025 have severely impacted women, children, the elderly, and displaced people, resulting in 64 million fewer individuals receiving aid. The global humanitarian aid system is facing a significant contraction due to shrinking contributions and job losses among aid workers, marking one of its largest...
summary.zh: 2025年的资金削减严重影响了妇女、儿童、老人和流离失所者，导致接受援助的人数减少了6400万。由于捐助减少和援助人员失业，全球人道主义援助系统正面临严重收缩，这是自二战后建立以来最大的萎缩之一。

body.en: Funding cuts in 2025 left women, children, older and displaced people hard hit, with 64m fewer people receiving aid The humanitarian aid system is crumbling as funding shrinks, pressures increase and governments not only fail to protect civilians but are increasingly responsible for endangering them, a new report warned on Thursday as figures revealed 64 million fewer people received aid last year. With aid contributions cut by 30% between 2022 and 2025 and thousands of aid workers losing their jobs, the humanitarian system has suffered one of its biggest contractions since being formed in the post-second world war era, according to the State of the Humanitarian System 2026 report. Continue reading...
body.zh: 2025 年的资金削减使妇女、儿童、老年人和流离失所者受到严重打击，接受援助的人数减少了 6400 万人随着资金减少、压力增大，以及政府不仅未能保护平民，而且对危及平民的责任越来越大，人道主义援助系统正在崩溃，周四的一份新报告警告说，数据显示去年接受援助的人数减少了 6400 万人。根据《2026 年人道主义系统状况》报告，2022 年至 2025 年间，援助捐款减少了 30%，数千名援助人员失业，人道主义系统遭受了自二战后时期形成以来最严重的收缩之一。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The report paints a grim picture of a humanitarian system struggling under financial strain, leaving millions of the most vulnerable without essential support. This crisis underscores the urgent need to advocate for those whose voices are often unheard, ensuring their basic needs are met and their dignity is upheld.
reflection.zh: 报告描绘了人道主义援助系统在财政压力下挣扎的严峻景象，使最脆弱的数百万人得不到基本支持。这场危机凸显了为那些常常无人倾听的声音发声的紧迫性，确保他们的基本需求得到满足，并维护他们的尊严。

verse.textEn: Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for the rights of all who are destitute. Speak up and judge fairly; defend the rights of the poor and needy.
verse.textZh: 你当为不能自辩的开口，为孤独的伸冤。你当开口按公义判断，为困苦和穷乏的辨屈。

title.en: Climate ‘feedback loops’ could worsen global warming by 30%, study finds
title.zh: 研究发现气候“反馈循环”可能使全球变暖加剧30%

summary.en: A new study indicates that rising global temperatures, driven by fossil fuel emissions, are causing natural environments like forests, wetlands, and tundra to release methane and CO2. These emissions from natural sources could potentially increase global warming by up to 30%, exacerbating the climate crisis.
summary.zh: 一项新研究表明，由化石燃料排放引起的气温上升正在改变森林、湿地和苔原等自然环境，使其释放甲烷和二氧化碳。这些来自自然源的排放物可能使全球变暖加剧多达30%，从而加剧气候危机。

body.en: Emissions of planet-heating methane and CO2 from natural sources are worsening the climate crisis, paper says Rising global temperatures caused by the burning of fossil fuels are transforming the world’s forests, wetlands and tundra to the point they are releasing emissions that could further worsen global heating by as much as 30%, a new study has found. As the world heats up, permafrost in the high latitudes is thawing, fiercer wildfires are burning in drying forests and wetlands and lakes are warming. All of these changes are themselves causing the release of planet-heating methane and carbon dioxide locked in trees and soils, therefore worsening the climate crisis, the paper states. Continue reading...
body.zh: 一项新的研究发现，自然资源排放的导致全球变暖的甲烷和二氧化碳正在加剧气候危机，化石燃料燃烧导致的全球气温上升正在改变世界森林、湿地和苔原，其排放量可能进一步使全球变暖进一步恶化30%。随着世界变暖，高纬度地区的永久冻土正在融化，干燥的森林中野火正在燃烧，湿地和湖泊正在变暖。该论文指出，所有这些变化本身都会导致树木和土壤中锁存的甲烷和二氧化碳的释放，从而导致全球变暖，从而加剧气候危机。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The earth itself, in its intricate systems of forests, wetlands, and tundra, groans under the impact of human-caused warming. As these natural 'feedback loops' accelerate the crisis, we are reminded that creation is deeply affected by our actions. May we approach this reality with humility and a renewed commitment to care for the planet entrusted to us.
reflection.zh: 大地本身，在其复杂的森林、湿地和苔原系统中，因人类引起的气候变暖而发出呻吟。当这些自然的“反馈循环”加速危机时，我们被提醒，受造界深受我们行为的影响。愿我们以谦卑的态度面对这一现实，并重新致力于照顾托付给我们的地球。

verse.textEn: We know that the whole creation has been groaning as in the pains of childbirth right up to the present time.
verse.textZh: 我们知道，一切受造之物一同叹息、劳苦，直到如今。

title.en: Hospitality industry fears jobs at risk from plan to give mayors powers to impose ‘tourist tax’
title.zh: 酒店业担心“旅游税”计划可能导致失业

summary.en: The hospitality industry is concerned about reports that there will be no cap on the levy that mayors can impose, following proposals by mayors like Andy Burnham and Steve Rotheram to introduce an overnight visitor levy.
summary.zh: 酒店业担心，据报道，市长们可以征收的税款将没有上限，此前安迪·伯纳姆和史蒂夫·罗瑟勒姆等市长提出了征收过夜游客税的计划。

body.en: The sector is concerned by reports that there won’t be a cap on the levy that can be imposed by mayors Good morning. Last year Andy Burnham, who was then mayor of Greater Manchester, and his close friend and ally Steve Rotheram, mayor of the Liverpool city region, were urging the government to allow mayors in England to bring in what they called a visitor levy. Burnham and Rotheram were pushing at an open door. In May this year Keir Starmer included plans for an overnight visitor levy bill in the king’s speech. Continue reading...
body.zh: 该行业对市长征收的征税不会设定上限的报道感到担忧。早上好。去年，时任大曼彻斯特市长的安迪·伯纳姆（Andy Burnham）和他的密友兼盟友利物浦城市地区市长史蒂夫·罗瑟拉姆（Steve Rotheram）敦促政府允许英格兰市长征收他们所谓的游客税。伯纳姆和罗瑟拉姆正在推开一扇敞开的门。今年 5 月，凯尔·斯塔默 (Keir Starmer) 在国王的讲话中纳入了过夜游客征税法案的计划。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The proposed 'tourist tax' raises concerns for the hospitality industry, particularly regarding its potential impact on jobs. This situation calls for careful consideration of how economic policies affect livelihoods. Micah 6:8 reminds us of the importance of acting justly, loving mercy, and walking humbly with God, principles that should guide decisions...
reflection.zh: 拟议的“旅游税”引起了酒店业的担忧，特别是其对就业的潜在影响。这种情况需要仔细考虑经济政策如何影响生计。弥迦书6:8提醒我们，要秉持公义、喜爱怜悯、谦卑行走，这些原则应指导那些影响企业和工人的决策。

verse.textEn: What does Yahweh require of you? To act justly and to love mercy and to walk humbly with your God.
verse.textZh: 雅伟向你所要的是什么呢？只要你行公义，好怜悯，存谦卑的心，与你的神同行。

title.en: How ancient teeth are changing what we know about early drug use
title.zh: 古代牙齿如何改变我们对早期药物使用的认知

summary.en: Scientists suggest that ancient humans may have utilized a nut with psychoactive properties for pain relief, based on new research.
summary.zh: 科学家根据新的研究表明，古代人类可能曾使用一种具有精神活性特性的坚果来缓解疼痛。

body.en:
A study of the teeth of ancient hunter-gatherers shows they sucked on betel nuts, evidence that humans used mind-altering drugs much earlier than previously thought, scientists say.

The Griffith University study, led by Professor Adam Brumm, examined teeth from two skeletons found on the Indonesian island of Sulawesi.

One dated from 16,000 to 25,000 years ago and the other from 6,300 to 7,600 years ago.

Their teeth showed unusual deep and rounded grooves that archaeologists established were caused by previously unknown drug-use behaviour — the habitual sucking of betel nuts, possibly for pain relief.

The betel or areca nut is a palm seed from Southeast Asia and is the fourth most commonly used psychoactive substance in the world, behind alcohol, caffeine and nicotine.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

It is mixed with slaked lime powder and chewed to boost its psychoactive properties and create a powerful stimulant.

But adding lime came after the time of the ancient hunter-gatherers, with Brumm saying it's thought they sucked betel nuts for pain relief.

"We think this was a longstanding cultural tradition of drug use that predated the invention of betel nut chewing as we know it today," he told the Australian Associated Press.

"We think this is how humans discovered the mind-altering properties of this particular type of drug."

It was the earliest evidence of the deliberate consumption of a psychoactive plant product but also the earliest evidence of habitual drug use, Brumm said.

Continuous betel-nut sucking wore down the teeth of ancient users, leading to cavities and intense pain, prompting more use of the nut for pain relief in an addictive cycle, he said.

"We can't exclude that they were getting a psychoactive hit but ... we don't think they were cavemen getting high on sucking betel nut."

Over time, ancient people discovered they could make a more potent stimulant if they chewed betel nut mixed with slaked lime, inducing mild euphoria and heightened alertness.

It had been thought the world's first traditions of psychoactive drug use arose after the Neolithic advent of farming, beginning with fermented barley beer about 13,000 years ago in what is now Israel.

The study's findings suggest habitual psychoactive substance use, and its associated health costs, were already present among hunter-gatherers tens of thousands of years before agriculture, Brumm said.

It reminds us that wisdom and understanding of the natural world, including its medicinal properties, have been sought since antiquity, often through careful observation and...

verse.textEn: But ask the animals, and they will teach you, or the birds in the sky, and they will tell you; or speak to the earth, and it will teach you, or let the fish in the sea inform you.
verse.textZh: 你且问走兽，走兽必指教你；又问空中的飞鸟，飞鸟必告诉你。或与地说话，地必指教你；海中的鱼也必向你说明。

title.en: Trump says every adult American would get $5,000 if Republicans win midterms
title.zh: 特朗普称若共和党赢得中期选举，每位成年美国人将获得5000美元

summary.en: Speaking at a party convention, the US president gave no details on how the plan would work or where the money would come from.
summary.zh: 美国总统在一次党派大会上发表讲话，但没有提供该计划如何运作或资金来源的细节。

body.en:
US President Donald Trump says he would offer every adult American a $5,000 (£3,700) payout if Republicans win both chambers of Congress in November's midterm elections - a plan that would cost more than a trillion dollars.

The controversial offer was made in a speech at the party's first-ever convention in the middle of a US presidential term.

He gave no details on how the plan would work or where the money would come from - saying only that the money would have to be spent in the US.

Democrats quickly labelled it an "empty promise" and others questioned whether such a pledge was legal.

There are nearly 270 million American adults, which means a $5,000 payout would cost the US government some $1.3 trillion.

Questions about whether his plan was possible have started to be asked - especially as prices rise in the US - partially as a result of the consequences of the war that the US and Israel started with Iran in February.

Iran's retaliation has included attacks against US bases and allies in the Gulf - but crucially it has largely closed the Strait of Hormuz where about a fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas used to transit.

The blockage has caused fluctuation in oil prices worldwide and Trump has faced pressure from his party to end the war.

On Wednesday, the US president warned his supporters that the war would not end until after the midterms and that oil prices would not come down until then.

He made the comments ahead of his speech in Texas, repeating it at the convention where he argued that short-term economic pain was worth it to prevent Tehran from developing nuclear weapons.

Trump's long speech at the Republican convention in Dallas, Texas, touched at the core of the conflict - the impact on the Americans' standard of living and his pledge to increase their spending power drew raucous applause in the hall.

"If the Republicans win the House of Representatives and the United States Senate, both of them," Trump said, "I will issue a dividend to every adult citizen in the United States of America for $5,000."

"We don't want you going to China, to Germany. You got to spend the money in the United States of America." It is not clear how the spending would be monitored.

It is not the first time that Trump promised such payouts - he has previously proposed $2,000 cheques to be funded by tariff revenues.

Other US politicians in the past have also promised economic rewards in return for electoral success.

For instance, Democrats in Georgia promised $2,000 relief payments if their party took control of the Senate at the height of the Covid-19 pandemic.

body.zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普表示，如果共和党在 11 月中期选举中赢得国会参众两院，他将为每位成年美国人提供 5,000 美元（3,700 英镑）的奖金，这一计划将花费超过 1 万亿美元。 这一有争议的提议是在美国总统任期中期举行的该党首次代表大会上的演讲中提出的。 他没有详细说明该计划将如何运作或资金从何而来，只是说这笔钱必须在美国使用。 民主党人很快将其称为“空头承诺”，其他人则质疑这样的承诺是否合法。 美国有近 2.7 亿成年人，这意味着 5,000 美元的支出将使美国政府损失约 1.3 万亿美元。 人们开始质疑他的计划是否可行，尤其是在美国物价上涨的情况下，部分原因是美国和以色列二月份与伊朗发动的战争所造成的后果。 伊朗的报复行动包括袭击美国在海湾的基地和盟友，但最重要的是，它基本上关闭了霍尔木兹海峡，世界上约五分之一的石油和液化天然气都用来运输该海峡。 封锁导致全球油价波动，特朗普面临党内要求结束战争的压力。 周三，美国总统警告他的支持者，战争要到中期选举之后才会结束，油价在此之前不会下跌。 他在德克萨斯州发表演讲之前发表了上述言论，并在大会上重申了这一点，他认为为了阻止德黑兰发展核武器，短期的经济痛苦是值得的。 特朗普在得克萨斯州达拉斯举行的共和党全国代表大会上发表的长篇演讲触及了冲突的核心——对美国人生活水平的影响以及他提高美国人消费能力的承诺，在会场赢得了热烈的掌声。 特朗普表示：“如果共和党赢得众议院和参议院的控制权，我将向美国每一位成年公民发放 5000 美元的股息。” “我们不希望你去中国、德国。你必须把钱花在美利坚合众国。”目前尚不清楚如何监控支出。 这并不是特朗普第一次承诺支付此类款项——他此前曾提议通过关税收入提供 2000 美元的支票。 过去其他美国政客也曾承诺以经济奖励来换取选举的成功。 例如，佐治亚州的民主党人承诺，如果他们的政党在 Covid-19 大流行最严重的时候控制参议院，将提供 2,000 美元的救济金。 在美国，国会授权支出，总统在达拉斯的演讲中没有透露他是否计划就这些付款请求此类批准 - 他...

However, the lack of detail on funding and implementation raises concerns about its practicality and potential for being an empty promise. reflection.zh: 如果共和党赢得中期选举，向每位成年美国人发放5000美元的承诺是一个大胆的说法。然而，缺乏资金来源和实施细节的说明，引发了对其可行性和可能成为空头支票的担忧。这呼应了圣经中关于警惕欺诈行为的告诫，提醒我们在所有财务事务中都要追求诚信和透明，尤其是那些影响公共利益的事情。

title.en: Five dead and 86 missing as 'heartbreaking' fire breaks out on Philippines ferry
title.zh: 菲律宾渡轮起火致五人死亡，86人失踪

summary.en: A fire broke out on the MV June Aster ferry in the Philippines, killing at least five people and leaving 86 missing. The vessel, carrying 117 passengers and 17 crew, was nearing its destination in Coron, Palawan, when the blaze started on Wednesday evening and was still burning on Thursday morning. Strong currents and...
summary.zh: 菲律宾一艘名为“六月艾斯特”号（MV June Aster）的渡轮发生火灾，已造成至少五人死亡，另有86人失踪。该渡轮载有117名乘客和17名船员，于周三晚间起火，周四上午火势仍在燃烧。据报道，强劲的水流和浓烟阻碍了灭火工作。一名幸存者称他在海中漂浮了两小时才获救。

body.en:
At least five people have died and 86 are missing after a fire broke out on a ferry in the Philippines, the country's coastguard said.

The MV June Aster, which set off from Manila ferrying 117 passengers and 17 crew members, was nearing its destination at the tourist hotspot of Coron when it caught fire.

The blaze, which erupted at 18:45 local time (10:45 GMT) Wednesday, was still burning as of 11:00 on Thursday. The strong currents and thick smoke were a challenge to those working to extinguish it, the coastguard said.

A survivor says he was in the sea for two hours before he got rescued. "It was cold. If the rescue was delayed, I would definitely have died," Roland Lerma told the BBC.

Video clips shared by the coastguard on Wednesday night showed the vessel engulfed in flames and people being pulled out of the water into rescue boats.

The coastguard said preliminary interviews with the survivors suggest the fire started in the cargo hold, which is the compartment where containers and or goods are stored, the coastguard said. Some passengers were not wearing life vests, they noted.

Forty-three people have been rescued but it is unclear how many have sustained injuries.

Seven of the survivors were taken to a hospital in Culion, a larger neighbouring island, which has higher bed capacity and more comprehensive healthcare services.

A first responder told the BBC they had never seen such a disaster in Coron, calling it "really heartbreaking".

"I was one of the people who carried and transported the casualties to the hospital last night," they said, adding that the ferry was an hour away from its destination.

The survivors were taken to an evacuation centre in Barangay Turda, which sits just north of Marcilla. The state of their injuries is unclear.

Her husband Marlon had spent a few days in Manila visiting their two children, who were going to school in the capital city.

Magbanua last heard from him while the ferry was passing through a village about two hours from the port in Coron, she tells the BBC.

"I was expecting that the ferry will arrive at the pier at between 18:00 and 19:00 yesterday," she said, adding that she had gone to bed early but was awakened by a cousin who told her the ferry Marlon was on had caught fire.

"I couldn't describe what I am feeling right now. I have been crying and praying since last night," Magbanua says.

She'd travelled to a hospital in Coron, hoping to find Marlon among the survivors – but he remains unaccounted for.

"My two-year-old son and I are outside the hospital as we speak. We have nothing but ourselves," she says.

Mae Lorraine Galera-Navoa, who is the sister of Garcia's brother-in-law, had travelled to Luzon to attend her father's funeral, accompanied by her husband Elyzer Navoa and their...
body.zh: 菲律宾海岸警卫队称，菲律宾一艘渡轮发生火灾，造成至少 5 人死亡、86 人失踪。 MV June Aster 号从马尼拉出发，载有 117 名乘客和 17 名船员，在接近目的地旅游胜地科隆时起火。 大火于周三当地时间 18:45（格林威治标准时间 10:45）爆发，截至周四 11:00 仍在燃烧。海岸警卫队表示，强劲的海流和浓烟对灭火工作人员来说是一个挑战。 一名幸存者说，他在海里呆了两个小时才获救。罗兰·勒玛告诉英国广播公司：“天气很冷。如果救援延误，我肯定会死。” 海岸警卫队周三晚间分享的视频片段显示，该船被火焰吞没，人们被从水中拉入救援船。 海岸警卫队表示，对幸存者的初步采访表明，火灾是从货舱开始的，货舱是存放集装箱和/或货物的隔间。他们指出，一些乘客没有穿救生衣。 四十三人已获救，但尚不清楚有多少人受伤。 其中七名幸存者被送往附近较大岛屿库利昂的一家医院，那里有更多的床位和更全面的医疗服务。 一名急救人员告诉英国广播公司，他们从未在科隆见过如此灾难，称其“真的令人心碎”。 他们说：“我是昨晚将伤员运送到医院的人之一。”他们补充说，渡轮距离目的地有一个小时的路程。 幸存者被送往位于马西拉北部图尔达描笼涯的一个疏散中心。他们的伤势尚不清楚。 她的丈夫马龙在马尼拉呆了几天，看望他们正在首都上学的两个孩子。 马格巴努阿最后一次听到他的消息是在渡轮经过一个村庄时，距离科隆港口约两小时车程，她告诉英国广播公司。 她说：“我预计渡轮会在昨天 18:00 至 19:00 之间抵达码头。”她补充说，她很早就睡觉了，但被表弟叫醒，表弟告诉她马龙乘坐的渡轮着火了。 “我无法描述我现在的感受。从昨晚开始我就一直在哭泣和祈祷，”马格巴努阿说。 她前往科隆的一家医院，希望在幸存者中找到马龙，但他仍然下落不明。 “我们说话时，我两岁的儿子和我正在医院外面。除了我们自己，我们一无所有，”她说。 梅·洛林·加莱拉·纳沃亚 (Mae Lorraine Galera-Navoa) 是加西亚姐夫的妹妹，她在丈夫埃利泽·纳沃亚 (Elyzer Navoa) 和他们的家人的陪同下前往吕宋参加她父亲的葬礼。

reflection.en: The news of the ferry fire, with its tragic loss of life and missing persons, brings to mind the deep human longing for an end to suffering. Revelation 21:4 speaks of a future where death will be no more, and mourning, crying, and pain will cease. While this earthly tragedy is heartbreaking, the biblical vision offers a profound hope for ultimate healing...
reflection.zh: 菲律宾渡轮火灾的消息，带来了生命的悲剧和失踪人员的痛苦，这触及了人类对终结苦难的深切渴望。启示录21:4 预言了未来“不再有死亡，也不再有悲哀、哭泣、疼痛”。尽管这世间的悲剧令人心碎，但圣经的应许却为最终的医治和复兴提供了深刻的盼望。

verse.textEn: He will wipe every tear from their eyes. There will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain.
verse.textZh: 神要擦去他们一切的眼泪；不再有死亡，也不再有悲哀、哭号、疼痛。

title.en: Iran war won't end until after crucial November elections, says Trump
title.zh: 特朗普称伊朗战争将在11月大选后结束

summary.en: US President Donald Trump stated that the conflict with Iran will not conclude until after the November midterm elections, predicting that oil prices will also remain high until then. He suggested, without providing evidence, that Iran aims to influence the election outcome.
summary.zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普表示，与伊朗的冲突要到11月中期选举后才能结束，并预测油价在此之前也将保持高位。他声称，伊朗希望影响选举结果，但未提供证据。

body.en:
US President Donald Trump has said he does not think the Iran war will end until after November's midterm elections, adding that oil prices will not come down until then.

"I think the war's going to end immediately after the election because they can't hold out any longer," Trump said of Tehran on Wednesday.

He made the comments as he headed to Texas for the party's first-ever midterm election convention - and repeated it there, arguing that short-term economic pain was worth it to prevent Tehran from developing nuclear weapons.

Trump is facing falling polling numbers and pressure from within his Republican Party to end the war with Iran.

"Right after the election, oil prices are going to be tumbling downward," Trump told reporters. "I think it's going to take a little bit longer than the midterm."

He added that Iran was "desperate to try and affect the election, so that we can get a nice weak group of people in there" - an apparent reference to the Democrats - "and leave them alone and let them have their nuclear weapon".

He provided no proof of the election claim. Tehran has repeatedly denied it is seeking nuclear weapons.

At the convention in Texas, Trump echoed some of these lines, saying the price of oil would tumble "as soon as we win the war with Iran".

In his speech, he also referenced dissatisfaction among some Americans on the issue: "Guys come up to me and say, 'I wish you didn't do the war in Iran. Now gasoline is up'".

Trump also said further negotiations with Iran could possibly happen, "but it's not something we're looking at".

The US president initially predicted the war, which is now in its seventh month, would last only a matter of weeks. The conflict, and its knock-on effects on everything from fuel to groceries, has led to a steep decline in his approval ratings - and pressure from those within his party, including devout supporters, to quickly end the war.

Midterm elections will be held on 3 November, and Republicans are in danger of losing their control on Congress.

At the convention, Trump sought to energise the party ahead of November. Historically, a sitting president's party tends to lose seats in Congress in the midterm elections.

Fighting in the Middle East has intensified in recent days, as oil facilities throughout the region come under attack, driving up the global price of fuel and any item that requires shipping.

The price of oil hit $100 a barrel on Wednesday for the first time since July. Similarly, earlier this week the price of US diesel hit an all-time-high , which is likely to cause a ripple effect on prices across the US.

body.zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普表示，他认为伊朗战争要到 11 月中期选举之后才会结束，并补充说在那之前油价不会下跌。 “我认为战争将在选举后立即结束，因为他们无法再坚持下去了，”特朗普周三谈到德黑兰时说道。 他在前往得克萨斯州参加该党有史以来第一次中期选举大会时发表了上述言论，并在那里重申了这一点，认为为了阻止德黑兰发展核武器，短期的经济痛苦是值得的。 特朗普面临着民意调查数字下降和共和党内部要求结束与伊朗战争的压力。 特朗普对记者表示：“大选结束后，油价将暴跌。” “我认为这会比中期选举需要更长的时间。” 他补充说，伊朗“不顾一切地试图影响选举，这样我们就可以在那里找到一群软弱的人”——显然是指民主党——“然后别管他们，让他们拥有核武器”。 他没有提供选举主张的证据。德黑兰一再否认正在寻求核武器。 在得克萨斯州举行的大会上，特朗普回应了其中一些观点，称“一旦我们赢得与伊朗的战争”，石油价格就会暴跌。 在演讲中，他还提到了一些美国人对此问题的不满：“人们走到我面​​前说，‘我希望你不要在伊朗发动战争。现在汽油涨价了’”。 特朗普还表示，可能会与伊朗进行进一步谈判，“但这不是我们正在考虑的事情”。 美国总统最初预测，目前已进入第七个月的战争将只持续几周。这场冲突及其对从燃料到食品杂货等各个领域的连锁反应，导致他的支持率急剧下降，并导致党内人士（包括虔诚的支持者）施压，要求他迅速结束战争。 中期选举将于11月3日举行，共和党面临失去对国会控制权的危险。 在大会上，特朗普试图在 11 月之前为党注入活力。从历史上看，现任总统所在的政党往往会在中期选举中失去国会席位。 最近几天，中东的战斗愈演愈烈，整个地区的石油设施受到攻击，推高了全球燃料和任何需要运输的物品的价格。 周三，油价自 7 月以来首次触及每桶 100 美元。同样，本周早些时候美国柴油价格创下历史新高，这可能会对美国各地的价格产生连锁反应。 周三，美国军方表示袭击了五艘与伊朗有联系的油轮。作为回应，德黑兰对两艘美国海军驱逐舰和八艘石油...

title.en: Serbia, the conflicted EU candidate
title.zh: 塞尔维亚，这个陷入冲突的欧盟候选国

summary.en: Serbia has officially pursued EU membership for years, but its accession process has stalled significantly. The recent state-supported funeral for convicted war criminal Ratko Mladic in Belgrade has highlighted the deep disconnect between Serbia's actions and European values, raising questions about its commitment to...
summary.zh: 塞尔维亚多年来正式寻求加入欧盟，但其入盟进程已严重停滞。最近在贝尔格莱德为被判刑的战犯拉特科·姆拉迪奇举行的国家支持的葬礼，凸显了塞尔维亚的行为与欧洲价值观之间的深刻脱节，并对其加入欧盟的承诺及其政治方向提出了质疑。

body.en:
On paper, Belgrade has pursued EU membership for years. But accession has long been stalled. The hero's farewell given to war criminal Mladic exposed just how far Serbia has alienated itself from Europe.

The  state-supported funeral of Ratko Mladic in Belgrade this week has raised a pressing question in Brussels: Can a country seek EU membership while giving a hero's farewell to a convicted war criminal? For many , the event has shown that Serbia's accession process has not merely stalled. It has largely lost its political drive.

"For too long, the EU has kept treating Serbia  as a normal candidate country," Engjellushe Morina of the European Council on Foreign Relations told DW, despite Belgrade's continued backsliding on democracy and the rule of law.

Naim Leo Besiri of Serbia's Institute for European Affairs adds: "The ruling majority in Serbia has not performed anything that was promised on the reform agenda during the last five years."

Both experts point out that Belgrade has refused to join EU sanctions against Russia . Democratic standards have deteriorated under nationalist President Aleksandar Vucic , while relations with Kosovo remain tense.

Despite having been sentenced to life imprisonment by a UN court for genocide, crimes against humanity and war crimes,  Ratko Mladic was buried in Belgrade on Monday with military honors and the participation of government representatives. President Vucic stayed away, but facilitated and defended the public mourning.

Brussels reacted unusually strongly. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen called the images shocking. European Council President Antonio Costa condemned the glorification of war criminals. Enlargement Commissioner Marta Kos canceled a visit to Serbia.

But both Morina and Besiri say that this is not enough. They believe Vucic has been given too much room to maneuver for too long. In their perception,  he has been treated as an indispensable partner who could secure stability in the Western Balkans and keep Serbia anchored to the West, despite disregarding basic European values.

Besiri says Serbian civil society had warned Brussels for years about attacks on media freedom, the rule of law and democratic institutions. But, he adds, the EU largely turned a blind eye.

Economic relations demonstrate the strong ties between the EU and Serbia. The bloc is Serbia's largest trading partner, investor and financial donor. Politically, however, Serbia has developed a close partnership with Moscow.

A common argument for continuing relations with Serbia is therefore based on the concern that greater pressure could push the country further towards Russia or China.

Morina accepts that isolating Serbia would be dangerous, but sees other options between...
body.zh: 从表面上看，贝尔格莱德多年来一直在寻求加入欧盟。但加入进程却长期停滞不前。这位英雄与战犯姆拉迪奇的告别暴露了塞尔维亚与欧洲的疏远程度。 本周在贝尔格莱德举行的由国家支持的拉特科·姆拉迪奇葬礼在布鲁塞尔引发了一个紧迫的问题：一个国家能否在寻求加入欧盟的同时，向一名被定罪的战犯进行英雄般的告别？对于许多人来说，这一事件表明塞尔维亚的入盟进程不仅停滞不前。它在很大程度上已经失去了政治动力。 欧洲外交关系委员会的莫里纳（Engjellushe Morina）对德国之声表示：“长期以来，欧盟一直将塞尔维亚视为正常的候选国。”尽管贝尔格莱德在民主和法治方面持续倒退。 塞尔维亚欧洲事务研究所的纳伊姆·利奥·贝西里 (Naim Leo Besiri) 补充道：“塞尔维亚的执政多数派在过去五年中没有履行改革议程上的任何承诺。” 两位专家都指出，贝尔格莱德拒绝加入欧盟对俄罗斯的制裁。在民族主义总统亚历山大·武契奇的领导下，民主标准有所恶化，而与科索沃的关系仍然紧张。 尽管拉特科·姆拉迪奇因种族灭绝罪、反人类罪和战争罪被联合国法院判处无期徒刑，但他仍于周一在贝尔格莱德以军事荣誉和政府代表的参与下葬。武契奇总统没有出席，但为公众哀悼提供了便利和辩护。 布鲁塞尔的反应异常强烈。欧盟委员会主席乌苏拉·冯德莱恩称这些图像令人震惊。欧洲理事会主席安东尼奥·科斯塔谴责美化战犯的行为。扩大事务专员玛尔塔·科斯取消了对塞尔维亚的访问。 但莫里纳和贝西里都表示这还不够。他们认为武契奇长期以来被给予了太多的回旋余地。在他们看来，他被视为不可或缺的合作伙伴，可以确保西巴尔干地区的稳定，并使塞尔维亚锚定在西方，尽管他无视欧洲的基本价值观。 贝西里表示，塞尔维亚民间社会多年来一直就针对媒体自由、法治和民主机构的攻击向布鲁塞尔发出警告。但他补充道，欧盟基本上对此视而不见。 经济关系体现了欧盟与塞尔维亚之间的牢固联系。该集团是塞尔维亚最大的贸易伙伴、投资者和财政捐助者。然而，在政治上，塞尔维亚与莫斯科建立了密切的伙伴关系。 因此，继续与塞尔维亚保持关系的一个常见理由是担心更大的压力可能会促使该国进一步向俄罗斯或中国靠拢。 莫里纳承认孤立塞尔维亚是危险的，但他认为还有其他选择……

reflection.en: The news from Serbia presents a stark image of a nation at a crossroads, its aspirations for European integration complicated by the honoring of a convicted war criminal. This situation raises profound questions about leadership and national identity. When a nation's leaders and public sentiment elevate those who have committed atrocities, it signals a deep...
reflection.zh: 塞尔维亚的新闻描绘了一个处于十字路口国家的鲜明图景，其对欧洲一体化的渴望因对被判刑的战犯的尊崇而变得复杂。这种情况引发了关于领导力和国家认同的深刻问题。当一个国家的领导人和公众舆论推崇犯下暴行的人时，这标志着在追求正义与和平方面存在着深刻的裂痕，阻碍了其迈向更统一、更公正未来的步伐。

verse.textEn: When the righteous thrive, the people rejoice; when the wicked rule, the people groan.

title.en: Donald Trump's 'only condition' for $5,000 payments to every American
title.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普向每位美国人支付5000美元的“唯一条件”

summary.en: President Donald Trump has pledged to pay every adult American $5,000 if Republicans maintain control of Congress in the upcoming midterm elections. This "Trump dividend" proposal, which could cost over $1.35 trillion, has raised questions about its funding source, which the president has not specified.
summary.zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普承诺，如果共和党在即将到来的中期选举中继续控制国会，将向每位成年美国人支付5000美元。这项“特朗普红利”的提议可能耗资超过1.35万亿美元，但总统尚未明确其资金来源，引发了相关疑问。

body.en:
President Donald Trump said on Thursday he would pay every US adult a US$5,000 ($6,926) "Trump dividend" if Republicans retain control of Congress in November's midterm election, an extraordinary attempt to persuade voters to back his party.

"If the Republicans win, you win with us, and you get $5,000. It will be called the Trump dividend," he told the Republican midterm convention audience in Dallas, Texas.

Trump likened the payments to a corporation's distributions to shareholders, citing "our tremendous strength and success economically".

He did not say where the money would come from — with the theoretical bill likely topping US$1.35 trillion ($1.85 trillion) — citing only that "our country is making so much money".

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

The promise would require congressional approval, and would further exacerbate the country’s nearly US$1.8 trillion annual budget deficit and concerns about inflation.

The payment would also come with a catch — Trump was clear he only wanted US citizens spending their prospective windfalls at home.

"But the only condition on the payment of this dividend that we’re going to be making … is that it must be spent in the United States of America," Trump told the convention crowd.

"We don’t want you going to Canada to spend the money. We don't want you going to China, to Germany. We got to spend the money in the United States of America."

Trump did not say how he and his administration would ensure the funds were only spent in the US.

During a primetime address that lasted an hour and 45 minutes, Trump boasted of completing "the greatest two years in the history of the presidency", putting himself squarely at the centre of the election despite his deepening unpopularity.

But it was not clear whether his campaign-style speech would appeal to the critical swing voters who opinion polls show have drifted away from Trump's party, amid growing dissatisfaction with the cost of living and the war on Iran.

"We hand America's future to the radical left Democrats, and our nation will spend the next decade just getting back on its feet," he said. "Vote Republicans, and we will leave the world in our dust for generations to come."

Within an hour, vice president JD Vance appeared to try to walk back Trump’s proposal — at least in part — by suggesting the dividend payments would not go to the wealthy. Vance suggested it could be paid for by US tariff revenues , though the suggested payment dwarfs what the US has taken in through the protectionist measures.

The US Congress would need to approve or otherwise acquiesce to the payment. The...
body.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普总统周四表示，如果共和党在 11 月中期选举中保留对国会的控制权，他将向每个美国成年人支付 5,000 美元（6,926 美元）的“特朗普红利”，这是说服选民支持他的政党的非凡尝试。 “如果共和党赢了，你们和我们一起赢了，你们会得到 5,000 美元。这将被称为特朗普红利，”他在德克萨斯州达拉斯举行的共和党中期大会上对观众说。 特朗普将这些付款比作公司向股东的分配，并引用了“我们巨大的实力和经济上的成功”。 他没有透露这笔钱从哪里来——理论上的账单可能会超过 1.35 万亿美元（1.85 万亿美元）——只是说“我们的国家赚了这么多钱”。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 这一承诺需要国会批准，并将进一步加剧该国近 1.8 万亿美元的年度预算赤字和通胀担忧。 这笔付款还有一个条件——特朗普明确表示，他只希望美国公民将未来的意外之财花在国内。 “但我们将要支付的股息的唯一条件......是它必须在美利坚合众国花费，”特朗普对大会人群说。 “我们不希望你去加拿大花钱。我们不希望你去中国、德国。我们必须把钱花在美利坚合众国。” 特朗普没有透露他和他的政府将如何确保这些资金只用在美国。 在长达一小时四十五分钟的黄金时段讲话中，特朗普吹嘘自己完成了“总统任期历史上最伟大的两年”，尽管他的不受欢迎程度日益加深，但他将自己置于选举的中心。 但目前尚不清楚他的竞选风格演讲是否会吸引关键的摇摆选民，民意调查显示，由于对生活成本和伊朗战争的不满日益加剧，这些选民已逐渐远离特朗普的政党。 他说：“我们将美国的未来交给激进的左翼民主党人，我们的国家将在未来十年重新站起来。” “投票给共和党，我们将把世界留给子孙后代。” 一个小时之内，副总统 JD 万斯似乎试图推翻特朗普的提议——至少部分推翻——暗示股息不会流向富人。万斯表示，这笔费用可以由美国关税收入来支付，尽管这一建议的支付金额使美国通过保护主义措施所获得的收入相形见绌。 美国国会需要批准或以其他方式默许这笔付款。这...

reflection.en: The promise of a "Trump dividend" of $5,000 to every American adult is presented as a reward for electoral success. This raises questions about the role of government and its responsibility to its citizens, beyond political patronage. Jeremiah 22:3 calls rulers to "execute justice and righteousness, and deliver from the hand of the oppressor him who suffers...
reflection.zh: 承诺向每位美国成年人支付5000美元的“特朗普红利”，被描绘成对选举成功的奖励。这引发了关于政府角色及其对公民责任的疑问，超越了政治恩惠。耶利米书22:3呼吁统治者“施行公平和公义，拯救被欺压的脱离欺压者的手”。这一原则提醒我们，领导力的真正衡量标准在于它如何服务于所有人的福祉和正义。

verse.textEn: Do what is just and right. Rescue from the hand of the oppressor the one who has been robbed.
verse.textZh: 你们要施行公平和公义，拯救被抢夺的脱离欺压人的手。

title.en: Russia outpacing Ukraine's air defences with daily use of new jet-powered drones
title.zh: 俄罗斯使用新型喷气式无人机，速度超过乌克兰的防空拦截能力

summary.en: Russia has been using new, fast, jet-powered drones daily throughout August, according to BBC analysis of Ukrainian Air Force data. These drones travel up to 300mph, faster than Ukraine's interceptors, leading President Zelensky to condemn the "unfolding horror." Drone attacks increased significantly from June to...
summary.zh: 根据英国广播公司对乌克兰空军数据的分析，俄罗斯在整个八月份每天都在使用新型、快速的喷气式无人机。这些无人机速度高达每小时300英里，超过了乌克兰的拦截能力，导致泽连斯基总统谴责这是“正在发生的恐怖”。无人机袭击次数从六月到八月显著增加。

body.en:
Russia fired its new rapid, jet-powered drones against Ukraine every day throughout August, BBC Verify analysis of Ukrainian Air Force data has found, escalating its use of a weapon that Kyiv's air defences are struggling to deal with.

It marked the first time that daily attacks by Moscow's new upgraded Geran drones were recorded in Ukrainian Air Force data. The growing use of jet-propelled and other varieties of drones prompted President Volodymyr Zelensky to condemn what he called an unfolding "horror" over the skies of Kyiv.

Ukraine's military recently told the BBC that jet-powered drone attacks grew from 350 in June to 1,600 in July and 2,800 in August. In five of the nightly attacks in August, these drones outnumbered the older, slower models.

"The reason for turning to jet-powered drones is that they are much faster than the previous generation and it makes it much more difficult for Ukraine to intercept them," said Dr Marina Miron, an expert on military technology at King's College London.

The upgraded munitions can cruise at more than 300mph, significantly faster than older models and well beyond the top speed of Kyiv's interceptors. The drones are powered by turbojet engines, some of which, according to Ukrainian military intelligence, are sourced from China.

According to Zelensky, the drones were used as part of a wave of attacks that killed at least 12 people and injured 20 more on 1 September. Six of the casualties were railway workers after a depot was hit in Kyiv.

Earlier this year Ukraine showed relative success in countering Russian drones and was intercepting 94% of long-range drones, according to Zelensky . But the speed of the newer drones has prompted the latest round in Kyiv and Moscow's arms race. On 10 August, Ukraine's deputy head of military intelligence, Maj Gen Vadym Skibitskyi, said his forces needed new interceptor missiles "capable of matching [jet-drones'] speed".

Four Ukrainian companies have reportedly started testing missiles that can shoot down the new Geran models, officials in Kyiv recently told reporters. The country's new defence minister, Yevhenii Khmara, has tasked them with producing "thousands of units" as quickly as possible.

Russia also had an economic incentive to invest in the jet-powered drones. The increased speed and manoeuvrability of these models means the line between them and more expensive cruise missiles has become "blurred", said John Hardie of the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, a think tank focused on national security and foreign policy.

"Long-range one-way attack drones are basically a poor man's cruise missile," he said. "The more you add capability to a drone, the less meaningful the distinction between the drone and a lower-end cruise missile."

But the analyst...
body.zh: 英国广播公司验证对乌克兰空军数据的分析发现，整个八月份，俄罗斯每天都向乌克兰发射新型快速喷气动力无人机，从而升级了基辅防空系统难以对付的武器的使用。 这标志着乌克兰空军数据中首次记录了莫斯科新升级的杰兰无人机的日常攻击。喷气式无人机和其他类型无人机的使用越来越多，促使总统弗拉基米尔·泽伦斯基谴责基辅上空正在发生的“恐怖”事件。 乌克兰军方最近告诉 BBC，喷气式无人机袭击次数从 6 月的 350 次增加到 7 月的 1,600 次和 8 月的 2,800 次。在 8 月份的五次夜间袭击中，这些无人机的数量超过了较旧、速度较慢的型号。 伦敦国王学院军事技术专家玛丽娜·米龙博士说：“转向喷气式无人机的原因是它们比上一代速度快得多，这使得乌克兰拦截它们变得更加困难。” 升级后的弹药可以以超过 300 英里/小时的速度巡航，明显快于旧型号，并且远远超过基辅拦截弹的最高速度。这些无人机由涡轮喷气发动机提供动力，根据乌克兰军事情报机构的说法，其中一些发动机来自中国。 据泽伦斯基称，这些无人机是 9 月 1 日发动的一波袭击的一部分，造成至少 12 人死亡、20 人受伤。基辅的一个仓库遭到袭击，其中六名伤亡者是铁路工人。 泽连斯基表示，今年早些时候，乌克兰在对抗俄罗斯无人机方面表现​​出相对成功，拦截了 94% 的远程无人机。但新型无人机的速度引发了基辅和莫斯科的最新一轮军备竞赛。 8 月 10 日，乌克兰军事情报局副局长 Vadym Skibitskyi 少将表示，他的部队需要“能够与[喷气式无人机]速度相匹配”的新型拦截导弹。 基辅官员最近告诉记者，据报道，四家乌克兰公司已开始测试可以击落新杰兰型号的导弹。该国新任国防部长叶夫尼·赫马拉 (Yevhenii Khmara) 责成他们尽快生产“数千辆”。 俄罗斯也有投资喷气式无人机的经济动机。专注于国家安全和外交政策的智库保卫民主基金会的约翰·哈迪表示，这些型号的速度和机动性的提高意味着它们与更昂贵的巡航导弹之间的界限已经变得“模糊”。 “远程单向攻击无人机基本上是一种穷人的巡航导弹，”他说。 “为无人机添加的功能越多，无人机和低端巡航导弹之间的区别就越没有意义。” 但分析师...

reflection.en: The relentless daily use of advanced weaponry, described as an "unfolding horror" over Ukraine, speaks to the devastating reality of modern warfare. In times of persistent global conflict, where human efforts to establish peace seem outmatched, we can turn to the ancient promise that Yahweh will ultimately bring an end to war, making weapons useless.
reflection.zh: 先进武器无休止的每日使用，被描述为乌克兰上空“正在发生的恐怖”，这反映了现代战争的毁灭性现实。在持续的全球冲突中，当人类建立和平的努力似乎显得力不从心时，我们可以转向古老的应许：雅伟终将平息战争，使武器归于无用。

verse.textEn: He makes wars cease to the ends of the earth; he breaks the bow and shatters the spear.
verse.textZh: 他止息刀兵，直到地极；他折弓断枪。

title.en: Why Donald Trump's latest map has the North Atlantic on edge
title.zh: 特朗普的最新地图为何让北大西洋紧张起来

summary.en: A map posted by United States President Donald Trump, showing the US extending to include Greenland and Iceland, has drawn sharp reactions from North Atlantic governments. The president offered no explanation for the 'disturbing' post, which follows months of comments about potentially annexing Canada and acquiring...
summary.zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普发布的一张地图，显示美国领土延伸至格陵兰岛和冰岛，引起了北大西洋各国政府的强烈反应。总统未对此“令人不安”的帖子作出任何解释，此前他已就可能吞并加拿大和出于战略原因获取格陵兰岛发表了数月评论。

body.en:
A map posted by United States President Donald Trump has drawn sharp reactions from governments across the North Atlantic.

The image showed the US stretching across North America and extending north to include Greenland and Iceland.

But it came after months of comments about Canada becoming the 51st US state and repeated statements about taking control of Greenland, a self-governing territory within the Kingdom of Denmark.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Trump has repeatedly said the US should acquire Greenland, citing its strategic importance.

Greenland is geographically part of North America but politically linked to Europe through its relationship with Denmark. It has extensive self-government, while Denmark remains responsible for areas including foreign and defence policy.

The latest map prompted a strong response from Danish foreign minister Lars Løkke Rasmussen.

"It’s disturbing and, in many ways, completely inappropriate," he told Danish broadcaster DR on Wednesday.

He said the post showed that Trump still held what he described as a "maximalist vision" and added: "We need to rein that in."

Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen also stressed that Greenlanders had repeatedly said they did not want to become part of the US.

Iceland became part of the controversy after Trump repeatedly referred to Iceland instead of Greenland while discussing his plans.

The countries are relatively close geographically, with Iceland about 290km from Greenland, but Iceland is an independent country and a NATO member.

Iceland's foreign secretary Thorgerdur Katrín Gunnarsdóttir summoned US ambassador Billy Long after Trump's map was posted. According to Iceland's national broadcaster RÚV, she told him the post was unacceptable.

The controversy has also added to debate in Iceland over its relationship with Europe.

Its left-leaning coalition government put forward a referendum on whether to resume long-stalled EU membership negotiations, partly framed around strengthening ties with Europe amid geopolitical uncertainty.

Earlier this year, thousands of Icelanders signed a petition urging the government to reject him as ambassador after he joked about Iceland becoming the 52nd US state and himself becoming its governor.

His comments came as Trump was already drawing attention in the region with his repeated statements about Greenland and Canada.

Canada has also faced frequent comments from Trump about becoming part of the US.

The remarks have coincided with a trade war between Washington and Ottawa. Trump has also recently referred to Lake Ontario as "Lake America".

body.zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普发布的一张地图引起了北大西洋各国政府的强烈反应。 该图像显示美国横跨北美并向北延伸包括格陵兰岛和冰岛。 但此前几个月，有关加拿大成为美国第 51 个州的言论不断涌现，并多次声明要控制丹麦王国境内的自治领土格陵兰岛。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 特朗普多次表示，美国应该收购格陵兰岛，理由是其战略重要性。 格陵兰岛在地理上是北美的一部分，但在政治上通过与丹麦的关系与欧洲联系在一起。它拥有广泛的自治权，而丹麦仍然负责外交和国防政策等领域。 最新的地图引起了丹麦外交部长拉斯·洛克·拉斯穆森的强烈反应。 “这令人不安，而且在很多方面都是完全不合适的，”他周三告诉丹麦广播公司 DR。 他说，这篇帖子表明特朗普仍然持有他所说的“极简主义愿景”，并补充说：“我们需要控制这一点。” 丹麦首相梅特·弗雷德里克森也强调，格陵兰人曾多次表示，他们不想成为美国的一部分。 特朗普在讨论他的计划时多次提到冰岛而不是格陵兰岛后，冰岛成为争议的一部分。 两国地理位置较为接近，冰岛距离格陵兰岛约290公里，但冰岛是独立国家，也是北约成员国。 在特朗普的地图发布后，冰岛外交大臣索尔格杜尔·卡特林·古纳尔斯多蒂尔召见了美国大使比利·朗。据冰岛国家广播公司 RÚV 报道，她告诉他这个帖子是不可接受的。 这场争议也加剧了冰岛关于其与欧洲关系的争论。 其左倾联合政府就是否恢复长期停滞的欧盟成员资格谈判提出了公投，部分目的是在地缘政治不确定性的情况下加强与欧洲的关系。 今年早些时候，数千名冰岛人签署了一份请愿书，敦促政府拒绝他担任大使，因为他开玩笑说冰岛将成为美国第 52 个州，而他自己也将成为该州州长。 在他发表此番言论之际，特朗普多次就格陵兰岛和加拿大发表言论，已经引起了该地区的关注。 加拿大也经常面临特朗普关于成为美国一部分的评论。 此番言论恰逢华盛顿和渥太华之间的贸易战。特朗普最近还将安大略湖称为“美国湖”。 在他的北美地图的同一个周末......

reflection.en: The posting of a map that dramatically redraws national boundaries, without explanation, can stir anxieties and challenge established international relations. Such actions can be seen as a manifestation of pride or overreach, reminding us that "pride goes before destruction, and an arrogant spirit before a fall."
reflection.zh: 一张未经解释就大幅重绘国家边界的地图的发布，可能会引发焦虑并挑战既有的国际关系。此类行为可被视为骄傲或越权的体现，提醒我们“骄傲在灭亡之前，狂心在跌倒之前。”

verse.textEn: Pride goes before destruction, a haughty spirit before a fall.
verse.textZh: 骄傲在败坏以先；狂心在跌倒之前。

title.en: Zelenskyy's plane 'almost hit' by drone; Trump says Putin wants Ukraine deal
title.zh: 泽连斯基飞机险遭无人机袭击；特朗普称普京希望达成乌克兰协议

summary.en: Donald Trump stated that Russian President Vladimir Putin desires a peace deal, coinciding with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's visit to Oslo. Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre reported that Zelenskyy's plane was nearly struck by a drone while taking off from Moldova, though a Ukrainian presidency...
summary.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普表示，俄罗斯总统普京希望达成一项和平协议，这与乌克兰总统弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基访问奥斯陆的事件同时发生。挪威首相约纳斯·加尔·斯特勒报告称，泽连斯基的飞机在摩尔多瓦起飞时险些被无人机击中，但乌克兰总统办公室的一位消息人士淡化了风险，称这一说法“被夸大了”，并将其归因于摩尔多瓦和罗马尼亚空域的无人机警报。

body.en:
Ukraine and Moldova have played down claims from Norway's prime minister that a plane carrying Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy was almost hit by a drone as it flew to Oslo.

Jonas Gahr Støre told Norwegian public broadcaster NRK on Thursday AEST that Zelenskyy's plane was "almost hit by a drone when it was taking off from Moldova".

But a source in the Ukrainian presidency described the claim that Zelenskyy was at risk as "exaggerated".

"It was an alert in Moldova when a Russian (drone) entered Moldovan and Romanian airspace," the source told the Agence France-Presse news agency (AFP).

In Chisinau, government spokesman Dumitru Ciorici said Moldova closed its airspace on Tuesday afternoon just after 4.30pm local time due to a Russian drone that entered from the direction of Ukraine.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

"The airspace was closed to protect aircraft flying over Moldova at the time: three departures and four arrivals were delayed as a result," he added.

"After 1720 [5.20pm], the authorities confirmed that the drone had come down and exploded ... some 160km from Chisinau International Airport.

"Flight restrictions were then lifted. For the same reason, the plane of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy took off ... later than scheduled."

Zelenskyy arrived in Oslo on Tuesday evening and held talks with Støre, finance minister Jens Stoltenberg and foreign minister Espen Barth Eide on Norwegian military aid, including air-defence support, and civilian assistance.

On Wednesday, he joined a host of other foreign dignitaries at the funeral of Norway's King Harald, who died on 28 August aged 89 .

US President Donald Trump said on Thursday that he had a "great" conversation ‌with Russian President Vladimir Putin earlier in the week and that the ‌Russian leader wanted to make a deal to end the Ukraine war.

"He is wanting to make a deal, and if Zelenskyy is wanting to make a deal, that'd be very nice," ‌Trump told ‌reporters ⁠before boarding Air Force One en route to Dallas for the Republican National Convention.

Trump spoke over the phone with Putin on Tuesday, shortly after US special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner returned from a diplomatic swing through Moscow and Kyiv.

⁠The duo, who are in ‌charge of most major peace negotiations for the US, discussed potential proposals to bring the ‌war to a close.

Last month, Central Intelligence Agency director John Ratcliffe met with intelligence officials in Moscow, in part to encourage Russian officials to end their invasion.

Despite those efforts and Trump's statements, intelligence officials in the US,...
body.zh: 乌克兰和摩尔多瓦淡化了挪威总理的说法，即一架载有总统弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基的飞机在飞往奥斯陆时差点被无人机击中。 周四，乔纳斯·加尔·斯托尔 (Jonas Gahr Støre) 向挪威公共广播公司 NRK 表示，泽连斯基的飞机“在从摩尔多瓦起飞时差点被无人机击中”。 但乌克兰总统府的一位消息人士称，泽连斯基面临危险的说法“言过其实”。 消息人士告诉法新社（法新社）：“一架俄罗斯无人机进入摩尔多瓦和罗马尼亚领空，这是摩尔多瓦的警报。” 在基希讷乌，政府发言人杜米特鲁·西奥里奇(Dumitru Ciorici)表示，由于一架俄罗斯无人机从乌克兰方向进入，摩尔多瓦于当地时间周二下午4:30刚过就关闭了领空。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 他补充说：“当时为了保护飞越摩尔多瓦的飞机，空域被关闭：三架飞机起飞和四架飞机抵达因此被延误。” “1720 年之后，当局确认无人机坠落并爆炸……距离基希讷乌国际机场约 160 公里（100 英里）。 “随后取消了航班限制。出于同样的原因，乌克兰总统泽连斯基的飞机起飞……比预定时间晚。” 泽连斯基周二晚抵达奥斯陆，与斯托尔、财政部长延斯·斯托尔滕贝格和外交部长埃斯彭·巴特·艾德就挪威军事援助（包括防空支持和民事援助）举行会谈。 周三，他与其他外国政要一起参加了挪威国王哈拉尔的葬礼，哈拉尔国王于 8 月 28 日去世，享年 89 岁。 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普周四表示，他在本周早些时候与俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京进行了“精彩”对话，俄罗斯领导人希望达成协议以结束乌克兰战争。 “他想要达成协议，如果泽伦斯基想要达成协议，那就太好了，”特朗普在登上空军一号前往达拉斯参加共和党全国代表大会之前告诉记者。 周二，在美国特使史蒂夫·威特科夫和贾里德·库什纳结束莫斯科和基辅的外交周旋回国后不久，特朗普与普京通了电话。 负责美国大多数重大和平谈判的两人讨论了结束战争的潜在建议。 上个月，中央情报局（CIA）局长约翰·拉特克利夫在莫斯科会见了情报官员，部分原因是为了鼓励俄罗斯官员结束入侵。 尽管做出了这些努力并发表了特朗普的声明，美国、乌克兰和……的情报官员

reflection.en: Amidst the ongoing conflict in Ukraine, reports surface of near-miss incidents involving President Zelenskyy's aircraft, juxtaposed with statements suggesting a potential for peace talks. This situation underscores the delicate balance between active hostilities and the persistent pursuit of diplomacy, reminding us to pray for wisdom and courage for leaders...
reflection.zh: 在乌克兰冲突持续之际，有报道称泽连斯基总统的飞机险些遭遇事故，同时也有言论暗示和平谈判的可能性。这一局势凸显了持续的敌对行动与不懈的外交努力之间的微妙平衡，提醒我们要为在复杂地缘政治紧张局势中斡旋的领导人祈求智慧和勇气。

verse.textEn: If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.
verse.textZh: 若是能行，总要尽力与众人和睦。

title.en: Saudi-led coalition and Houthis trade strikes as Yemen conflict deepens
title.zh: 沙特领导的联盟与胡塞武装交火，也门冲突加剧

summary.en: Renewed fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis is raising fears of a return to broader conflict in the region. Hundreds have been killed in recent clashes near the Red Sea, with over 50 attacks targeting various regions in Yemen. Thousands have been displaced, with one individual describing the situation as a...
summary.zh: 沙特阿拉伯与胡塞武装之间的新一轮战斗加剧了该地区重返更广泛冲突的担忧。最近在红海附近的冲突已造成数百人死亡，超过50次袭击针对也门多个地区。数千人流离失所，其中一人形容局势为“一场灾难”。

body.en:
Houthi rebels and the Saudi-led coalition exchanged airstrikes overnight as daily attacks continued in a conflict that has reignited during the Middle East war, with hundreds of people killed in fighting near the Red Sea.

More than 50 attacks targeted several regions in Yemen, including the flashpoint areas of Taiz and Hodeida, the scene of fierce clashes between the Houthis and the Saudi-backed government, the rebels said.

"It's a catastrophe, and the attacks are ongoing," said Mohammed Khudairi, one of nearly 20,000 people who fled the fighting, according to the International Organization for Migration.

"We managed to leave, but others remain trapped there," he said at a displacement camp of wood-and-straw huts near Khokha, on the Red Sea coast.

The latest salvos in Yemen's previously dormant conflict come a day after the Houthis set oil sites ablaze and wounded 73 in their heaviest missile and drone attacks against Saudi Arabia in years.

The Saudi-led military coalition said the Iran-backed group had launched fresh attacks on the kingdom's south on Wednesday as the Houthis reported dozens of incoming salvoes from the kingdom.

The rebels' Al-Masirah TV channel reported on Wednesday the toll from Saudi strikes on a prison days earlier had climbed to 32 dead and seven injured as rescue and recovery efforts continued.

The fighting comes against the backdrop of the Middle East war, which erupted in late February with US-Israeli strikes on Iran .

The Middle East war has sucked in Yemen, the energy-rich Gulf and others across the region while roiling the world economy, as oil prices returned to $100 a barrel on Wednesday.

The fighting in Yemen has killed more than 500 people since the Houthis launched a major offensive last week to seize territory around the Bab al-Mandab strait, gateway to the Red Sea shipping route.

The rebels , who have been attacking Saudi oil tankers, are trying to tighten their squeeze on the shipments, analysts say — a lifeline for exports after Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz .

The Saudi-led coalition's spokesman Turki al-Maliki said the Houthis "launched several ballistic missiles and drones toward the cities of Khamis Mushait, Abha, and Jizan", without mentioning any casualties as a result of the attacks.

Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree had earlier said that "during the past 12 hours, the Saudi enemy's air force conducted 54 airstrikes targeting the provinces of Al-Jawf, Marib, Taiz, Hodeida and Saada".

Footage released by the group showed what it said were attacks on Saudi-backed forces on Al-Jawf province's frontlines, with missiles heard flying overhead...
body.zh: 胡塞叛军和沙特领导的联军隔夜相互空袭，中东战争期间冲突重新燃起，每日袭击仍在继续，红海附近的战斗造成数百人死亡。 叛乱分子称，也门多个地区发生了 50 多起袭击，其中包括塔伊兹和荷台达的热点地区，这里是胡塞武装与沙特支持的政府发生激烈冲突的地点。 据国际移民组织称，“这是一场灾难，袭击仍在继续”，穆罕默德·胡代里是逃离战斗的近 2 万人之一。 “我们设法离开，但其他人仍被困在那里，”他在红海沿岸科卡附近的一个由木头和稻草搭建的难民营中说。 也门此前休眠的冲突最近一次齐射是在胡塞武装对沙特阿拉伯发动多年来最严重的导弹和无人机袭击，纵火焚烧石油设施并造成 73 人受伤的一天之后。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 沙特领导的军事联盟表示，伊朗支持的组织周三对沙特南部发动了新的袭击，胡塞武装报告称，沙特发射了数十次齐射。 叛军的 Al-Masirah 电视频道周三报道称，随着救援和恢复工作的继续进行，几天前沙特对一所监狱的袭击造成的死亡人数已攀升至 32 人，7 人受伤。 这场战斗是在中东战争的背景下发生的，中东战争于二月底因美国和以色列对伊朗的袭击而爆发。 中东战争已经波及也门、能源丰富的海湾地区和该地区其他国家，同时扰乱了世界经济，油价周三重返每桶 100 美元。 自胡塞武装上周发起大规模攻势，夺取通往红海航线的曼德海峡周边领土以来，也门的战斗已造成 500 多人死亡。 分析人士称，一直在袭击沙特油轮的叛乱分子正试图加强对石油运输的挤压——这是伊朗关闭霍尔木兹海峡后出口的生命线。 沙特领导的联军发言人图尔基·马利基表示，胡塞武装“向海米斯穆谢特、艾卜哈和吉赞等城市发射了多枚弹道导弹和无人机”，但没有提及袭击造成的任何人员伤亡。 胡塞武装发言人叶海亚·萨里早些时候表示，“在过去12小时内，沙特敌方空军对焦夫、马里卜、塔伊兹、荷台达和萨达等省份进行了54次空袭”。 该组织发布的视频显示，据称他们对焦夫省前线的沙特支持部队发动了袭击，听到导弹从头顶飞过……

reflection.en: The news from Yemen paints a grim picture of escalating conflict and displacement. The cycle of airstrikes and counter-strikes, as described by Mohammed Khudairi and the thousands fleeing, traps civilians in a catastrophe. The ancient call to 'not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good' (Romans 12:21) offers a profound challenge to break these...
reflection.zh: 也门的新闻描绘了一幅冲突升级和流离失所的严峻景象。正如穆罕默德·胡代里和成千上万逃离者所描述的，空袭与反击的循环将平民困在灾难之中。《罗马书》12:21 呼吁“不要被邪恶打败，反而要用善来打败邪恶”，这为打破这些破坏性模式提供了深刻的挑战。

verse.textEn: Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.
verse.textZh: 你不可为恶所胜，反要以善胜恶。

title.en: China: English to be removed as a graded core subject?
title.zh: 中国：英语将从应试核心科目中移除？

summary.en: A university professor is advocating for English to be removed as a graded core subject in Chinese schools. Opponents argue that in a globalized world, proficiency in English is beneficial for the country and individual careers.
summary.zh: 一位大学教授呼吁在中国学校取消将英语作为有评分的核心科目。反对者认为，在全球化的世界中，掌握英语对国家和个人职业生涯都有益。

body.en:
A university professor is calling for English to no longer be taught as a graded core subject in Chinese schools. Opponents argue that, in a globalized world, knowing English benefits the country and one's career.

From business and academia to social media and entertainment — English is considered the dominant global language. One in five people on Earth actively uses this lingua franca. In China , a mathematics professor specializing in vector algebra is now challenging this dominance in no uncertain terms. Tang Jiafeng believes that English should be abolished as a core subject in elementary schools, secondary schools and universities.

Tang is convinced that no other country in the world has placed as much importance on English as China has.

"Our children desperately begin learning English even before they have properly mastered their native language. Yet we are a civilization that dates back thousands of years. English is just a tool. It's enough to be able to use it. The tradition of revering and emulating Western cultures must come to an end," Tang says in social media.

English is considered difficult in China, since the Chinese language does not use an alphabetic script. It is a required subject starting in third grade. It is graded on par with Chinese and mathematics on the entrance exam for secondary schools, the central exam after 9th grade, and the high school graduation exam. A maximum of 150 points can be earned on the latter.

"How many resources and how much time do our children, parents and schools invest in a subject that is completely irrelevant to the majority of people in their future professional lives?" the mathematician asks, explaining his position.

He became well-known because many of his students achieved full scores on state math exams; in the class of 2011, six students from a single class did so.

"Why cram for English when artificial intelligence can translate everything in seconds?" comments a user from Beijing.

Another suggestion from the southern province of Guangdong is to at least adjust the scoring — for example, to 120 points instead of 150 on the high school graduation exam.

Many parents invest in private tutoring that focuses specifically on exam questions. In addition, all bachelor's students must pass the English exam before being admitted to master's programs. Tang suspects that this could cause many young talents in the natural sciences to fail, even though they have great potential to become top researchers.

There is no question that English is also important for STEM subjects. Research on future-oriented topics is typically published in English. There are fears circulating online that cutting back on English instruction could lead to a decline in China's competitiveness. A prominent...
body.zh: 一位大学教授呼吁中国学校不再将英语作为分级核心科目来教授。反对者认为，在全球化的世界中，懂英语对国家和个人的职业生涯都有好处。 从商业和学术界到社交媒体和娱乐——英语被认为是全球主导语言。地球上五分之一的人积极使用这种通用语言。在中国，一位专门研究向量代数的数学教授现在正在毫不含糊地挑战这一主导地位。唐家峰认为，应该取消英语作为小学、中学和大学的核心科目。 唐坚信，世界上没有哪个国家像中国一样重视英语。 唐在社交媒体上表示：“我们的孩子在还没有真正掌握母语之前就拼命地开始学习英语。但我们是一个有着数千年历史的文明。英语只是一种工具，能够使用它就足够了。尊重和效仿西方文化的传统必须结束。” 英语在中国被认为很难，因为中文不使用字母文字。这是从三年级开始的必修科目。中学入学考试、九年级后的集中考试和高中毕业考试的成绩与语文和数学同等。后者最多可获得 150 点积分。 “我们的孩子、家长和学校在一个与大多数人未来职业生涯完全无关的主题上投入了多少资源和时间？”数学家问道，并解释了他的立场。 他之所以出名，是因为他的许多学生在州数学考试中取得了满分。 2011届的一个班有六名学生这样做了。 “当人工智能可以在几秒钟内翻译所有内容时，为什么还要死记硬背英语呢？”北京网友评论。 来自南方省份广东省的另一项建议是至少调整分数——例如，高中毕业考试的分数从150分调整为120分。 许多家长投资专门针对考试问题的私人辅导。此外，所有学士学生必须通过英语考试才能进入硕士课程。唐怀疑这可能会导致许多自然科学领域的年轻人才失败，尽管他们有成为顶尖研究人员的巨大潜力。 毫无疑问，英语对于 STEM 科目也很重要。面向未来的主题的研究通常以英文发表。网上流传着这样的担忧：削减英语教学可能会导致中国竞争力下降。一位杰出的...

reflection.en: The debate over English as a core subject in China touches on the purpose of education itself. Proverbs 1:7 reminds us that the fear of Yahweh is the beginning of knowledge, suggesting that true learning is rooted in a deeper wisdom than mere linguistic proficiency or career advancement.
reflection.zh: 关于英语在中国是否应成为核心科目的争论，触及了教育本身的目的。箴言1:7提醒我们，敬畏雅伟是知识的开端，这表明真正的学习根植于比单纯的语言能力或职业发展更深层次的智慧。

verse.textEn: The fear of Yahweh is the beginning of knowledge, but fools despise wisdom and instruction.
verse.textZh: 敬畏雅伟是知识的开端；愚妄人藐视智慧和训诲。

title.en: Germany's connection to the September 11, 2001 attacks
title.zh: 德国与“9·11”袭击事件的联系

summary.en: The 9/11 attacks were partly planned in Hamburg by the so-called Hamburg cell, whose members played key roles in the plot. This event prompted a significant shift in Germany's approach to national security.
summary.zh: “9·11”袭击事件的部分计划是在汉堡通过所谓的“汉堡小组”进行的，其成员在阴谋中扮演了关键角色。这一事件促使德国在国家安全方面采取了重大转变。

body.en:
The 9/11 attacks were partly planned in Hamburg, via the so-called Hamburg cell, whose members played key roles in the plot. A look back at a day that shook up Germany’s approach to national security.

"This day has changed the world," German President Johannes Rau said. He had watched in shock as the burning Twin Towers of the World Trade Center collapsed in New York.

Nearly 3,000 people were killed on September 11, 2001, when Islamist terrorists hijacked four passenger planes and turned them into deadly weapons.

Germany’s head of state struggled to find the right words: "We do not know what political or social consequences what happened today will have — what we have watched unfold on our television screens in shock, barely able to comprehend or even reflect on it."

It soon emerged that the victims include people from 92 countries, among them 11 Germans.

The following day, a rapidly spreading rumor was confirmed: Three of the four suspected hijackers had recently lived in Hamburg. The Islamist terrorists were thought to have been led by Egyptian-born Mohammed Atta, who had come to the northern German city in the early 1990s to study.

At some point, the young man became radicalized, particularly at Hamburg's Al-Quds Mosque, which was later closed by German security authorities. He spent the final three years of his life in an apartment shared with two other suspected attackers in the Harburg district.

The so-called Hamburg terrorist cell was believed to have included six men, among them Moroccan national Mounir al-Motassadeq. He was charged as an accomplice in the world's first trial related to the September 11, 2001, attacks . In 2003, the Hanseatic Higher Regional Court sentenced him to the maximum 15-year prison term for aiding and abetting thousands of murders and for membership in a terrorist organization.

After serving his sentence, al-Motassadeq was deported to his native Morocco. Another suspected attacker from the circle around pilot Mohammed Atta was Ramzi Binalshibh, who was born in Yemen and had been held without trial at the US detention facility at Guantanamo Bay since 2006.

The United States detained hundreds of suspects at the prison, which human rights groups and international bodies have described as contrary to international law. Among them was Murat Kurnaz , who was born in Bremen. He was released in August 2006 after nearly five years without evidence establishing his involvement in the terrorist attacks.

Kurnaz later recounted his experience in a book that was adapted into a film in 2013 .

Meanwhile, investigative committees in the German Bundestag sought to determine why Kurnaz and other suspects had wrongly come under the scrutiny of American and German intelligence...
body.zh: 9/11 袭击的部分计划是在汉堡通过所谓的汉堡小组策划的，该小组的成员在该阴谋中发挥了关键作用。回顾改变德国国家安全方针的一天。 “这一天改变了世界，”德国总统约翰内斯·劳说道。他震惊地看着纽约世贸中心双子塔燃烧着倒塌。 2001 年 9 月 11 日，伊斯兰恐怖分子劫持了四架客机并将其变成致命武器，造成近 3,000 人死亡。 德国国家元首努力寻找合适的措辞：“我们不知道今天发生的事情会产生什么政治或社会后果——我们震惊地看到电视屏幕上发生的事情，几乎无法理解，甚至无法反思。” 很快就有消息称，遇难者包括来自 92 个国家的人，其中包括 11 名德国人。 第二天，一个迅速传播的谣言得到证实：四名劫机嫌疑人中的三人最近住在汉堡。伊斯兰恐怖分子被认为是由埃及出生的穆罕默德·阿塔领导的，他于 20 世纪 90 年代初来到这座德国北部城市学习。 在某个时候，这位年轻人变得激进，特别是在汉堡的圣城清真寺，该清真寺后来被德国安全当局关闭。他在哈尔堡区与另外两名袭击嫌疑人合住的公寓里度过了生命的最后三年。 据信，所谓的汉堡恐怖分子组织包括六名男子，其中包括摩洛哥国民穆尼尔·莫塔萨德克(Mounir al-Motassadeq)。在世界上首例与 2001 年 9 月 11 日袭击有关的审判中，他被指控为共犯。 2003年，汉萨地区高等法院以协助和教唆数千起谋杀案以及恐怖组织成员身份判处他最高15年的监禁。 刑满释放后，穆塔萨德被驱逐回祖国摩洛哥。飞行员穆罕默德·阿塔周围的另一名疑似袭击者是拉姆齐·比纳尔什布 (Ramzi Binalshibh)，他出生于也门，自 2006 年以来未经审判就被关押在美国关塔那摩湾拘留所。 美国在该监狱拘留了数百名嫌疑人，人权组织和国际机构称此举违反了国际法。其中包括出生于不莱梅的穆拉特·库尔纳兹 (Murat Kurnaz)。近五年来，没有证据证明他参与了恐怖袭击，他于 2006 年 8 月被释放。 库尔纳兹后来在一本书中讲述了他的经历，该书于2013年被改编成电影。 与此同时，德国联邦议院的调查委员会试图确定为什么库尔纳兹和其他嫌疑人错误地接受了美国和德国情报部门的审查……

reflection.en: The 9/11 attacks, with roots in Hamburg, serve as a stark reminder of how acts of terror can reshape a nation's security posture and global outlook. The challenge remains to respond to such evil not with mirroring violence, but with a commitment to justice and peace, embodying the principle of overcoming evil with good.
reflection.zh: “9·11”袭击事件，其根源可追溯至汉堡，是恐怖行为如何重塑国家安全态势和全球视野的严峻警示。挑战依然在于，我们如何不以同等的暴力回应邪恶，而是以对公正与和平的承诺来克服邪恶，践行以善胜恶的原则。

verse.textEn: Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.
verse.textZh: 你不可为恶所胜，反要以善胜恶。

title.en: Iran tightens social control with crackdown on cafes
title.zh: 伊朗因担心助长反政府情绪而加强对咖啡馆的社会管控

summary.en: Iranian authorities have recently intensified their scrutiny of cafes in Tehran, viewing them as potential hubs for fostering anti-government sentiment and facilitating protests. On July 19 alone, at least seven cafes and restaurants were reportedly shut down for non-compliance with mandatory hijab regulations,...
summary.zh: 伊朗当局近期加强了对首都德黑兰咖啡馆的审查，认为它们可能助长反政府情绪并促进抗议活动。据人权组织HRANA称，仅在7月19日，就有至少七家咖啡馆和餐馆因未能遵守强制性头巾规定而被勒令关闭。

body.en:
Authorities are keeping a close eye on cafes, fearing they could play a role in fostering anti-government sentiment.

Iranian authorities have launched a clampdown on cafes in the capital, Tehran, in recent months, suspecting them of fostering anti-government sentiment and facilitating protests.  

According to the human rights organization HRANA, at least seven cafes and restaurants were shut down on July 19 alone for allegedly failing to comply with mandatory hijab rules.

Previously, some media outlets, including Javan , a newspaper affiliated with the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) , have described cafes as "gathering places for protesters" who, in their view, pose a threat to "national security."

Most recently, the "Vanak Park" cafes in Tehran were sealed, resulting in at least 200 people losing their jobs.

Authorities believe cafes, because of their widespread presence and popularity, could play a role in organizing mass protests.

The government's fears are rooted in the latest wave of protests in Iran, which began on December 28, 2025, and grew into the country's largest uprising since the 1979 Islamic Revolution.

Saediniya, a well-known cafe chain with 10 branches in Iran, closed its branches on this day in support of calls for strikes. It was subsequently accused of engaging in "propaganda against the state."

Iran's Supreme Court has now upheld the sentence of Sadegh Saedinia, the owner of the cafe chain, to 12 years and six months in prison, along with the confiscation of his assets.

He was arrested over his support for the protests, and all branches of his cafe chain were confiscated and shut down by judicial order.

Other cafes, including "Lamiz" and "Voria," faced a broadly similar fate. Voria is owned by a prominent Iranian footballer. Both were sealed by judicial order because of their indirect support for calls to protest. Cafe closures have not been confined to periods of protest, however, and the practice continues.

Tehran has seen a surge in the number of cafes over the past decade, rising from around 300 in the early 2010s to as many as 4,000 now, according to various estimates. 

Some experts attribute the growing number to changes in urban lifestyles in recent years. They see this as more than the expansion of a particular type of business and describe it as a sign of wider social and cultural changes within Iranian society.

"The explosive growth of cafes in society can, to some extent, be seen as a social response to living in a state of chronic crisis," Saba Alaleh, a clinical psychologist and psychoanalyst whose work focuses on political and social issues, told DW's Persian service.

"In such circumstances, people are not simply looking to consume or be entertained. They are looking for a...
body.zh: 当局正在密切关注咖啡馆，担心它们可能会助长反政府情绪。 近几个月来，伊朗当局对首都德黑兰的咖啡馆进行了取缔，怀疑它们煽动反政府情绪并为抗议活动提供便利。 据人权组织 HRANA 称，仅 7 月 19 日，就有至少 7 家咖啡馆和餐馆因涉嫌未遵守强制性头巾规定而被关闭。 此前，包括伊斯兰革命卫队（IRGC）下属报纸《爪哇报》在内的一些媒体将咖啡馆描述为“抗议者的聚集地”，他们认为抗议者对“国家安全”构成威胁。 最近，德黑兰“瓦纳克公园”咖啡馆被查封，导致至少200人失业。 当局认为，咖啡馆因其广泛存在和受欢迎而可以在组织大规模抗议活动中发挥作用。 政府的担忧源于伊朗最近一波抗议活动，该抗议活动始于2025年12月28日，并发展成为该国自1979年伊斯兰革命以来最大规模的起义。 在伊朗拥有10家分店的知名连锁咖啡馆Saediniya在这一天关闭了分店，以支持罢工的呼声。随后它被指控从事“反国家宣传”。 伊朗最高法院现已维持这家咖啡馆连锁店老板 Sadegh Saedinia 的刑期，判处 12 年零 6 个月监禁，并没收其资产。 他因支持抗议活动而被捕，他的咖啡馆连锁店的所有分店都被司法命令没收和关闭。 其他咖啡馆，包括“Lamiz”和“Voria”，也面临着大致相似的命运。 Voria 的所有者是一位著名的伊朗足球运动员。两人均因间接支持抗议呼吁而被司法命令封存。然而，咖啡馆关闭并不局限于抗议时期，而且这种做法仍在继续。 根据各种估计，过去十年德黑兰的咖啡馆数量激增，从 2010 年代初期的约 300 家增加到现在的 4,000 家之多。 一些专家将这一数字的增加归因于近年来城市生活方式的变化。他们认为这不仅仅是特定类型企业的扩张，并将其描述为伊朗社会内部更广泛的社会和文化变革的标志。 专注于政治和社会问题的临床心理学家和精神分析师萨巴·阿拉勒 (Saba Alaleh) 告诉德国之声波斯语频道：“社会上咖啡馆的爆炸式增长在某种程度上可以被视为对长期危机状态的社会反应。” “在这种情况下，人们不仅仅是为了消费或娱乐。他们正在寻找......

reflection.en: In Tehran, cafes are being targeted by authorities, with at least seven shut down for failing to enforce hijab rules. This action highlights a tension between state control and personal expression, raising questions about justice and freedom. The prophet Amos declared, 'Let justice roll on like a river, righteousness like a never-failing stream!' May we...
reflection.zh: 在德黑兰，咖啡馆正成为当局的目标，至少有七家因未能执行头巾规定而被关闭。这一行动凸显了国家控制与个人表达之间的紧张关系，并引发了对公正和自由的疑问。先知阿摩司曾宣告：“惟愿公平如大水滚滚，公义如江河滔滔！”愿我们祈祷，公正与自由能为所有人民带来繁荣。

verse.textEn: Let justice roll on like a river, righteousness like a never-failing stream!
verse.textZh: 惟愿公平如大水滚滚，使公义如江河滔滔。

The call to 'act justly' is a fundamental principle that guides our engagement with the world, urging us to consider the integrity and potential consequences of our...
reflection.zh: 亚历山大·切尔戈被判刑，这严厉提醒我们，我们的行为，即使是通过领英等职业网络发起的，也具有重大的道德分量。“秉公行义”的呼召是我们与世界互动的基础原则，敦促我们考虑工作的诚信和潜在后果，尤其是在涉及国家安全和国际关系的问题上。

verse.textEn: What does Yahweh require of you? To act justly and to love mercy and to walk humbly with your God.

verse.textEn: When the righteous thrive, the people rejoice; when the wicked rule, the people groan.
